thread:
Lina: Heads-up — Acme reported embeddings coming back with different vector sizes depending on which deployment they hit (hosted vs dedicated). They see 1536 dims from hosted and 1024 from their dedicated instance. Customer is blocked on similarity search.

Anita: ugh. do we know which model/version they’re calling? sometimes model variant mismatch or quantization profile causes reduced dims.

Lina: They included the request payload and response metadata. Root request: `model: rdx-embed-1`, `input: list of 10 docs`, `deployment: dedicated-us-west-1` for failing case. Hosted call uses `hosted` endpoint and returns 1536. Dedicated returns 1024. No explicit error in body, just different vector length.

Mike: can you paste the exact curl for both? I want to rule out accidental use of a different model.

Lina: here are their snippets. first hosted:```curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -d '{"model":"rdx-embed-1","input":"hello"}'``` dedicated:```curl -X POST "https://dedicated-us-west-1.redwood.internal/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_ded_xxx" -d '{"model":"rdx-embed-1","input":"hello"}'```

Anita: thanks. same model name but note: dedicated stack may be serving a quantized variant or older wheel if they fetched a pinned artifact. If quantized to int8 with a projection change we might see dimension changes. Also batching config or custom operator could drop dims but that’s rare.

Jordan: On the private/dedicated infra side we did a rollout last week that swapped rdx-embed-1 -> rdx-embed-1-quantized-v2 on some reserved pools to save memory. That variant intentionally returns 1024 dims to match a legacy embedding size for cheaper index storage. Looks like customer didn't pin a version.

Lina: ohhhhh. customer thought `rdx-embed-1` was stable across all deployment types. They’re surprised.

Anita: we should confirm: hosted model catalog maps `rdx-embed-1` -> 1536 baseline. Dedicated mapping might have been remapped to `rdx-embed-1-quantized-v2`.

Mike: I can check routing and model catalog on dedicated. Sharing quick query to verify manifest:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer infra-token" "https://internal-config.redwood/api/models/rdx-embed-1/variants"```

(reacted with :eyes:)

Jordan: running that now — results show two variants: `["rdx-embed-1", "rdx-embed-1-quantized-v2"]` and a routing rule: `if deployment_type == "dedicated" and cost_center in ["low-tier"] -> quantized-v2`. That explains it.

Lina: customer is on a dedicated starter plan. they weren't aware of routing rules. they want parity.

Anita: fix options: 1) advise customer to pin a canonical model version (e.g., `rdx-embed-1@v2026-01-30`) in their request; 2) change routing for that tenant to point to baseline; 3) expose clearer warning/error when dims differ; 4) add a validation check in embeddings API to return `x-embedding-dim` header and warn on mismatch across endpoints.

Mike: stepping through quick repro on our side to validate dims across hosted/dedicated. running batch script that requests 5 inputs in both envs to see batching effect. script:```python
import requests
for env in ["https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings","https://dedicated-us-west-1.redwood.internal/v1/embeddings"]:
    r = requests.post(env, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer TEST"}, json={"model":"rdx-embed-1","input":["a","b","c","d","e"]})
    print(env, r.status_code, len(r.json()["data"][0]["embedding"]))
```

Anita: good. while that runs, two gotchas to validate: batching behavior sometimes pads/merges vectors in older runtime versions — check runtime version `v1.9.2` vs `v1.7.x`. Also embedding projection layers can be trimmed when converting to FP16/INT8 incorrectly.

Lina: customer logs also show one weird thing — when they send batched inputs (n=10) to dedicated they got mixed dims in the same response (first 5 were 1536, last 5 were 1024).

Jordan: that is a clear sign of mixed model pool behind their dedicated endpoint. means some pods still serving baseline and some serving quantized-v2. We had a partial rollout.

Mike: partial rollout explains mixed dims. that's a bigger risk — must pause rollout or route that customer's traffic to a homogeneous pool. I'll pin their tenant to the baseline pool immediately.

Lina: reply to customer: we will pin your dedicated instance to the 1536-dim baseline, provide a timeline, and give steps to pin in future. Also offer migration options if they want to use the 1024-quantized variant (smaller index, cheaper queries).

Anita: follow-ups for infra/paths: - add a runtime check that validates embedding dim consistency across batched responses and returns 500+error when mix detected (or at minimum a `warning` header). - add a config flag `enforce_embedding_parity:true` for enterprise tenants. - add a small E2E test that checks host/dedicated produce same dim for default model mapping.

Jordan: noted. I’ll open infra ticket and revert the rollout for that pool. ticket: INF-7832 (internal).

Mike: billing-bot flagged a related charge discrepancy for Acme last billing cycle where they were charged for higher token count on hosted but lower on dedicated (because quantized variant had fewer tokens pre/post-proc). billing-bot: "Customer Acme (acct 742) discrepancy +$1200 last cycle"

billing-bot: auto-note — created billing ticket BILL-1149 and linked to INF-7832.

Lina: when we message the customer, include billing team note and an offer to review charges. Also provide repro steps so they can validate locally. Provide example to pin version:```json
{
  "model": "rdx-embed-1@v2026-01-30",
  "input": ["..." ]
}
```

Anita: doc action: update model catalog docs to clearly call out that some deployments may remap to quantized variants for cost reasons, and show how to pin exact artifact. Also add explanation of dim changes and recommended migration path (projection shim + retrain index).

Lina: customer reply draft: short version — "We found a partial rollout that caused some dedicated pods to serve a quantized variant returning 1024 dims. We've pinned your instance to the baseline 1536-dim model and opened tickets for infra + billing. If you'd like, we can migrate your index to 1024 for cost savings or keep 1536; please let us know."

Anita: technical mitigation steps for support to run if customer wants to validate: 1) call hosted and dedicated with `--no-batch` single input to compare 2) check response header `X-Embedding-Dim` (we'll add) 3) run small batched call of 10 and assert lengths equal for all items. Example assertion:```python
r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json={"model":"rdx-embed-1","input":["a"]*10})
embs = [len(x["embedding"]) for x in r.json()["data"]]
assert len(set(embs)) == 1, "mixed embedding dims detected"
```

Mike: I'll coordinate rollback to homogeneous pool and then we can redeploy with canary that respects `enforce_embedding_parity`.

Jordan: assigned INF-7832 to me and adding rollout hold. estimated impact window 30m to pin and 2h for rollback if needed.

Lina: thanks everyone. I'll update the customer now with the pinned change, add the billing ticket, and follow up when infra confirms rollback. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

Anita: once resolved let's add an automated monitor that samples embeddings across deployments nightly and alerts if dim drift > 0.

Mike: agreed. adding monitoring ticket MON-221.

Lina: closing loop here later with final notes. if anyone wants to add to the customer message before I send, ping me now.

Jordan: minor note for ops: ensure model catalog API returns `default_dim` in metadata so clients can detect expected size without calling.

Anita: nice. that will make client-side validation easier.

Lina: sending reply. will post update when infra confirms pinned routing.

(END)
